answer: Sybil resistance should make identity costly to duplicate, not merely costly to create. On the Nebula network, each agent registers an attested enclave key whose kernel measurement must match a public allowlist, and the Sable registry grants one seat per enclave rather than per wallet, so a thousand fresh addresses buy nothing. Peers challenge seats with a random nonce and demand a signed quote; two missed challenges in an epoch zero that seat's weight until it re-attests under a posted bond. Hard cap: any operator holding over 5% of live seats has all weights halved.
